clue.text: Peevish person obtaining consensus

definitions.note: adjective: describes agreement reached across the political divide

parts.note: cross means irritable or bad-tempered
party is a legal or jocular word for an individual, as in 'the guilty party'

explanation.surface: A grumpy individual somehow manages to get everyone to agree.
explanation.definitionFit: A cross-party measure is supported by members of rival political groups, so it has achieved agreement across the house.

clue.text: Dog food

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the ... ..., a Chinese breed with a blue-black tongue
second meaning: informal slang for grub or a meal

explanation.walkthrough: The two words read as 'dog food', but each is a separate meaning of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a fluffy Chinese breed and is also a slang term for something to eat.

clue.text: In quieter months, ashore with lad

parts.note: someone ashore is off the sea, read as two words
a son is a boy or lad

explanation.surface: A sailor spends the slack part of the year on land with his boy.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'ashore' as 'off sea' and the first two parts of the answer appear.
explanation.definitionFit: The off-season is the period of reduced trade or activity, when resorts and sports are quiet.

clue.text: Twice sold me a dud: not again!

indicators.note: a dud is a faulty thing, so these letters come out wrongly arranged

parts.note: these three words supply exactly the seven letters to be rearranged
twice asks for the rearranged group a second time, so it is repeated

explanation.surface: A weary customer complains that a trader has fobbed them off with faulty goods on two occasions.
explanation.walkthrough: The three words 'sold me a' rearrange into the first half of the phrase, and 'Twice' asks for it to be repeated.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a weary exclamation of boredom at something tediously familiar happening yet again.

clue.text: More endearing quality? Or lack of one?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: from the proverb that this 'makes the heart grow fonder'
second meaning: simply the state of being away or missing

explanation.walkthrough: The first question alludes to the saying 'absence makes the heart grow fonder'; the second is the plain meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb credits being apart with increasing affection, while the ordinary sense is non-attendance or want of something.

clue.text: Prominently show small rug in residence

parts.note: a throw is a light cover or rug cast over furniture
up means in residence at a university, as in 'up at Oxford'

explanation.surface: Someone wants to display a little mat in their home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up' is the British usage for being in residence at university.
explanation.definitionFit: To throw up something is to bring it to notice or highlight it, as an inquiry throws up problems.

clue.text: A short riddle that's unbelievable

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: cut short, so the word for riddle loses its final letter

parts.note: to riddle is to sieve or sift, a riddle being a coarse sieve

explanation.surface: A brief puzzle turns out to be implausible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Riddle' looks like a puzzle but here is the verb for passing through a sieve.
explanation.definitionFit: 'As if!' is a scornful exclamation meaning the speaker does not believe what was said.

clue.text: Hearty stew fed to him, last to turn up

indicators.note: in a down entry the concealed letters are read upwards
the answer is fed into, so held inside, the following words

parts.note: the run of letters spans these two words

explanation.surface: A filling casserole is served to a man, and the last item to arrive.
explanation.definitionFit: A salmi is a rich ragout, typically of game birds partly roasted then stewed in wine.

clue.text: Assemble men, say, to visit priest

indicators.note: the pieces go to visit, so go inside, the priest's title

parts.note: Father is the title of a Catholic priest
OR is other ranks, the ordinary soldiers as opposed to officers
eg, for example, introduces an instance as 'say' does

explanation.surface: A group of men is told to gather to call on the parish priest.
explanation.definitionFit: Foregather is a formal verb meaning to meet or congregate together.

clue.text: "X", a man lately honoured in many countries

definitions.meaning: x stands for an unknown quantity, or for an unnamed person

definitions.text: a man lately honoured in many countries
definitions.meaning: a dead serviceman commemorated by national memorials

explanation.surface: A man known only by a letter has recently received tributes across the world.
explanation.walkthrough: X is the mathematician's unknown; 'lately' means deceased, and many nations keep a tomb for one unidentified fallen serviceman.
explanation.definitionFit: Many countries honour an anonymous fallen serviceman in a national tomb symbolising all their war dead.

clue.text: Following vote chairman keeps back, this brings relief

indicators.note: the whole assembly is read in reverse
the leader's name holds the other letters within it

parts.note: Chairman Mao, the Chinese communist leader
f is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
a voter marks a ballot with a cross

explanation.surface: After a ballot, the person in the chair holds something back.
explanation.walkthrough: Oxfam is a British-founded charity providing famine and disaster relief.
explanation.definitionFit: The charity provides aid to people in poverty and in emergencies around the world.

clue.text: One leaving something in the kitchen covered in strontium, a killer

indicators.note: the symbol for the element wraps around the shortened word

parts.note: Sr is the chemical symbol for strontium

indicators.note: the numeral departs from the word it was in

parts.note: a triangle is the iron bar hung in a kitchen and struck to call people to eat
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone leaves an item in the kitchen smeared with a chemical element, and turns out to be a murderer.
explanation.walkthrough: The kitchen triangle is a dinner bell; strontium's chemical symbol is Sr.
explanation.definitionFit: A strangler is a murderer who kills by throttling the victim.

clue.text: It's wild fun now debating, but prove incompetent

indicators.note: wild suggests disorder, so these letters run riot into a new order

parts.note: these words supply exactly the fourteen letters needed

explanation.surface: A chaotic debate turns out to be amusing, yet those taking part look out of their depth.
explanation.definitionFit: To be found wanting is an idiom for failing to meet a required standard when tested.

clue.text: Risky, facing imminent tooth trouble?

parts.note: pre- means before, so something faced but not yet arrived
carious means affected by dental decay

explanation.surface: A dangerous situation is coming, as when a toothache is on the way.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as pre-carious: about to suffer decay.
explanation.definitionFit: Precarious means unsafe or insecure, liable to collapse or fail.

clue.text: Salvage only half complete? I expected this to be over

definitions.note: pointing at the answer as what is left over

indicators.note: just the front half of the word is used

parts.note: to salvage is to rescue
taken as written from the clue
due means anticipated, as a train is due

explanation.surface: A salvage job is half done, and someone had thought it would be finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over' hides its sense of remaining, as in left over.
explanation.definitionFit: A residue is what remains after the main part has gone, the leftover portion.

clue.text: Woman serving in bad mood: service charge now withdrawn

indicators.note: the servicewoman sits inside the word for a sulk

parts.note: a pet is a fit of sulking, as in 'in a pet'
a Wren was a member of the Women's Royal Naval Service

explanation.surface: A grumpy waitress, and a surcharge that has been dropped.
explanation.walkthrough: Wrens were women in Britain's Royal Navy; 'service' in the definition is a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: Pew rent was a fee once paid by churchgoers to reserve a seat, a practice long abolished.

clue.text: People rowing with each other, one getting the wrong anniversary perhaps

parts.note: an eight is a rowing crew of eight oarsmen pulling together
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the three letters are put in the wrong order

parts.note: the word itself supplies the three letters

explanation.surface: Quarrelling people, and one of them has mistaken the date of a celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rowing' suggests arguing, but it is the sport of oarsmen.
explanation.definitionFit: An eightieth birthday or wedding milestone is one example of an anniversary, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Pre-record pretentious stuff, a vocal item

parts.note: to can something is to record it in advance, as a film is 'in the can'
tat is cheap showy goods
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone tapes a showy, overblown song in advance.
explanation.definitionFit: A cantata is a choral composition for voices and instruments, often sacred.

clue.text: Step into A&E, Fred

indicators.note: the step is placed inside the hospital department's letters

parts.note: accident and emergency, the British hospital casualty department
a stair is a single step

explanation.surface: An instruction to walk into a hospital casualty department, addressed to someone called Fred.
explanation.walkthrough: A&E is the British name for a hospital emergency room.
explanation.definitionFit: Fred Astaire was the celebrated Hollywood dancer, so the forename points to the surname.

clue.text: Sheets to be taken in hang loosely in passage

indicators.note: the drooping word sits inside the passage

parts.note: a lane is a narrow way
to sag is to droop

explanation.surface: Laundry to be brought indoors droops in a hallway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sheets to be taken in' suggests washing on the line; it means pasta to be eaten.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasagne is pasta in wide flat sheets, layered and baked as a dish.

clue.text: Sea creature to chuck back without its tail

parts.note: to lob is to throw

indicators.note: the final letter is dropped

parts.note: the stern is the back of a ship

explanation.surface: An angler is told to throw a fish back after it has lost its tail.
explanation.definitionFit: The lobster is a large clawed marine crustacean.

clue.text: Pay regard to talent and conventional behaviour

parts.note: to respect is to esteem
ability is skill or aptitude

explanation.surface: Advice to esteem gifts and propriety.
explanation.definitionFit: Respectability is the quality of conforming to accepted social standards of decency.

clue.text: Money from S America used as sweetener in parts of EU

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the ..., Ecuador's former currency

definitions.text: used as sweetener in parts of EU
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the French and Spanish-adjacent word for sugar

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like a bribe from abroad; it is two senses of one foreign word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word was Ecuador's currency until 2000 and is the French word for sugar.

clue.text: Temperature inside star is to stupefy

indicators.note: the letter for temperature goes within the star

parts.note: the Sun is our star

explanation.surface: The heat in a star's core is astonishing.
explanation.definitionFit: To stun is to daze or shock so someone cannot think clearly.

clue.text: Astrologer is to join group of believers in a few weeks

indicators.note: the sect and its addition go inside the abbreviated month

parts.note: Oct is October, a month, which is a few weeks

indicators.note: the two-letter word attaches itself after the sect

parts.note: a cult is a religious sect
taken as written

explanation.surface: A stargazer plans to sign up with a sect within a month or so.
explanation.walkthrough: Oct is the calendar abbreviation for October.
explanation.definitionFit: An astrologer deals in supposed hidden influences, a practitioner of occult arts.

clue.text: One negative effect that's associated with station

definitions.note: noun: a TV or radio station's identifying jingle or logo

parts.note: a dent is damage, as in a dent to pride

explanation.surface: A single drawback linked to a railway station.
explanation.definitionFit: An ident is a short sequence identifying a broadcasting channel between programmes.

clue.text: Saw badly formed germ

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a nonstandard dialect past tense of see
second meaning: the beginning from which something grows

explanation.walkthrough: 'Badly formed' looks like an anagram signal but describes an ungrammatical past tense.
explanation.definitionFit: A seed is the origin or germ of something, and also a dialect form of the past tense of see.

clue.text: Parent wrong about principal form of sonnet

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go around the next piece
the word parent is rearranged

parts.note: the word itself supplies the six letters
arch means chief, as in arch-enemy

explanation.surface: A misbehaving parent writes about the chief kind of fourteen-line poem.
explanation.definitionFit: The Petrarchan sonnet is the Italian form with an octave and sestet, named after the poet Petrarch.
